items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: from my buddy Dick Sudhalter, who I went to high school with

ctx.x: When did this twentieth century, for lack of a better term, classical music enter into your thinking?

You know I can’t remember a time when it wasn’t there because when I was going to school, and I mean now let’s see it wouldn’t be grammar school, probably junior high school, I used to have, you know people use coffee timers for their coffee? My coffee timer was for my phonograph. So I would wake up and the phonograph would go on, and I would listen to maybe Woody Herman’s Third Herd, followed by Alban Berg’s “Lulu © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Suite”, followed by maybe Spike Jones, followed by Art Tatum. So the mixture of things was always churning. It wasn’t until so many years later that what I actually realized was it was all about sound. That’s what interests me. I mean melody interests me greatly also, especially because it’s connected to the heart. But what is the sound of that melody? So the sound spectrum is what interests me. And I like to listen to a whole bunch of different people that treat the sound spectrum in different ways. Like…
